title: Jailer 2 to Open With 6 AM Shows in Kerala, Bookings From October 11
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel gets a record-scale Kerala rollout from Sree Gokulam Movies, with more than 4,000 shows targeted on opening day and the superstar returning as Muthuvel Pandian on October 15.
body:
• Rajinikanth’s “Jailer 2” will begin its Kerala run with 6 AM first shows on October 15, the film’s worldwide release day, with advance bookings opening on October 11 at 10 AM IST.
  • Sree Gokulam Movies is distributing the film in Kerala — with Dream Big Films as its distribution partner — after acquiring the rights for a record sum, and trade reports point to a target of more than 4,000 opening-day shows across the state.
  • Nelson Dilipkumar directs the sequel, with Rajinikanth returning as Muthuvel Pandian alongside Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Vidya Balan, S.J. Suryah, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Jackie Shroff and Mithun Chakraborty, and music by Anirudh Ravichander.
  • Kerala fans can book from 10 AM on October 11; overseas advance bookings in markets including the US and UK are already open, so diaspora viewers can lock in premiere seats now rather than waiting.

A record-scale Kerala rollout

“Jailer 2” is headed for one of the biggest theatrical releases Kerala has seen for a Tamil film. The sequel’s first shows in the state are scheduled for 6 AM on October 15, while advance booking opens four days earlier, on October 11 at 10 AM IST — giving exhibitors and the trade a clear window to gauge initial demand.

The Kerala release is being handled by Sree Gokulam Movies, which acquired the film for a record sum, with Dream Big Films as its distribution partner in the state. The distributor is preparing a large-scale rollout, with trade reports indicating a target of more than 4,000 shows in Kerala on opening day — a figure that should be treated as a reported target rather than a final count.

Why 6 AM matters

The 6 AM start is significant for a Rajinikanth film in Kerala, where early-morning first shows have long been central to the superstar’s opening-day theatrical culture. Fans traditionally turn the first-day-first-show into a celebration, and the pre-dawn slot lets the film pack in as many as six shows per screen on day one, according to Kerala box office trackers.

The film has cleared its certification formalities: “Jailer 2” has received a U/A 16+ certificate with an approved runtime of 165 minutes and 18 seconds — just under two hours and 46 minutes.

The film itself

Nelson Dilipkumar’s film released its trailer earlier this week, offering the first extended look at Rajinikanth’s return as Muthuvel Pandian. The sequel pulls the retired jailer back into conflict with the criminal underworld after his family and legacy come under threat.

The ensemble is the film’s biggest draw beyond its home market. Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar, who made special appearances in the first “Jailer,” return — Mohanlal as Mathew, Shiva Rajkumar as Narasimha — with the trailer’s high-octane Mohanlal appearance driving exceptional excitement among Kerala audiences. Suraj Venjaramoodu plays Dileep, positioned as a key antagonist, alongside Vidya Balan, S.J. Suryah, Jackie Shroff, Mithun Chakraborty, Yogi Babu and Hakkim Shajahan. Anirudh Ravichander returns as composer, continuing his collaboration with Nelson and Rajinikanth after the first “Jailer.”

An aggressive final push

The Kerala booking announcement lands as the film enters the final stretch of its pre-release campaign. Rather than the traditional large-scale audio launch associated with Rajinikanth’s films, the makers have opted for a different promotional route this time — including a three-hour television interview with the superstar ahead of release — while the film’s music has been rolled out in the run-up to opening day.

Sree Gokulam Movies is also handling the film’s Karnataka distribution, alongside K Manju Cinemas, extending its footprint across the South. The trade is already measuring the film against a stiff benchmark: the first “Jailer” delivered one of the biggest runs ever recorded by a Tamil movie in Kerala, and analysts are watching whether the sequel can challenge the territory records set by recent blockbusters.

What to watch

With bookings opening October 11, the first real signal will be how fast the opening-day shows sell through. A record Kerala opening would confirm “Jailer 2” as the season’s biggest theatrical bet — and set the tone for the film’s worldwide run starting October 15.
